chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from a shaykh among the people of al-Kūfah, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him and said: “May I be your ransom, a man entered the house of some people, and their dog sprang at him inside the house and wounded him.” So he said: “If he had been invited, then the compensation for the scratch is upon the people of the house; but if he had not been invited, then there is nothing upon them.”

key_terms.أَرْشُ: financial compensation assessed for an injury
key_terms.دَارَ: house or dwelling in which the incident occurred
key_terms.دُعِيَ: he was invited or permitted to enter
key_terms.فَعَقَرَهُ: it wounded him or inflicted injury upon him
key_terms.كَلْبُهُمْ: their dog, the animal that caused the injury

ai.seo_question: Is the owner liable if a guest is injured by their dog inside the house?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding liability when a person is injured by a householder’s dog inside the home. If the injured person entered by invitation, the residents are liable for compensation; if he entered without being invited, they bear no liability.
